conventions.convention: Extremal length λ is the supremum of squared family length divided by density area over Borel densities with finite positive area; curve-family modulus μ is 1/λ, with 1/0=∞ and 1/∞=0. Empty families have λ=∞; families containing a constant path have λ=0.

Densities are extended by zero outside the domain. Rectifiable-path length uses the atomless arclength Stieltjes measure; nonrectifiable compact paths are assigned infinite density length. Boundary endpoints contribute no mass.

Analytic quasiconformality requires W1,2 locally and the weak inequality |f_barz|≤k|f_z|, where k=(K−1)/(K+1)<1. ACL alone or an almost-everywhere classical derivative inequality does not replace the Sobolev condition. These analytic items assume AC; the extremal-length interfaces assume Countable Choice.

Geometric quasiconformality includes orientation preservation, defined by the positive local integral-homology multiplier for the standard plane orientation (1,i), as well as both modulus inequalities.

The coefficient μ_f is set to zero where f_z=0. For a general Sobolev homeomorphism, finite maximal dilatation additionally requires f_barz=0 almost everywhere on that set; coefficient zero alone is insufficient.

Annular end paths are proper maps (0,1)→A with tails escaping into different exhaustion ends. Weighted length is the supremum of compact-restriction integrals, allowing local rectifiability and nonlanding tails.

A sphere coefficient is chartwise, with source pullback μ∘ψ times conjugate(ψ′)/ψ′. In the infinity chart w=1/z, μ_infinity(w)=μ_0(1/w)w²/conjugate(w)². The value at w=0 is immaterial; weak test pairings are bilinear.
Normalized sphere solutions fix 0,1,∞. Unnormalized quasiconformal homeomorphic solutions differ by Möbius postcomposition. A non-quasiconformal homeomorphic limit is assigned maximal dilatation ∞.

Hölder results use integer regularity order ≥0 and 0<α<1. The Cauchy transform is T=−4∂zN with N built from −(2π)−1 log|z|; its derivative kernel is −1/(πz²), with circular principal values and subtraction only inside the unit disk.

Quasisymmetry uses both orders of adjacent equal intervals or arcs. The inverse has controlled quasisymmetry, without asserting the same adjacent-arc constant. A uniform disk-boundary restriction constant requires |H(0)|≤r<1; a line-preserving sphere map must fix infinity, and either its restriction or its negative is increasing.

Global conformal removability tests sphere homeomorphisms conformal off a compact set and concludes Möbius. Its neighborhood-local equivalence is proved under AC. The finite-length analytic removability result covers finite chordal H1, including zero H1.

Welding uses an ordered pair of complementary components and h=f−1∘g on their common boundary, equivalently g=f∘h. This is the inverse of the cited source convention. Simultaneous Möbius postcomposition leaves h unchanged.

The metric-to-analytic bridge has one bounded owner-authorized citation exception: qualitative regularity only. I checked [Gehring](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0027763000024272), pp.175–179 and §14, against F4 and research/frontier-43-complex-representation-15-circular-metric-citation-authorization.json. The paper states the equivalence and refers its proof elsewhere; the sharp L bound remains locally derived.

The zero-area nonremovable Jordan comparison uses the separate owner-authorized original existence input. I checked [Bishop](https://www.acadsci.fi/mathematica/Vol19/bishop.pdf), Theorem 2, its following paragraph, the radius-gauge definition and §§3–4, against F7 and research/frontier-43-complex-representation-15-bishop-comparison-citation-authorization.json. The gauge is prescribed first; witnesses may depend on it. The item uses h(t)=t² and proves the diameter-cost conversion locally.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, an analytically K-quasiconformal homeomorphism of complex domains gives both K-distortion bounds for relatively compact quadrilateral joining families and for the specified annular end-path families. For every relatively compact Borel E, area(f(E))=∫E J_f; in particular its inverse maps null Borel sets to null sets.

Under AC, for a homeomorphism between complex domains and each K≥1, orientation preservation together with both K-quadrilateral modulus bounds is equivalent to local W1,2 regularity and |f_barz|≤((K−1)/(K+1))|f_z| almost everywhere. Least constants agree; inverses have the same maximal dilatation.

Under AC, an orientation-preserving analytically K-quasiconformal homeomorphism gives K−1μ(Γ_Q)≤μ(Γ_f(Q))≤Kμ(Γ_Q) for every relatively compact Jordan quadrilateral and either marked pair. No inverse regularity, inverse-null property or arbitrary-ring comparison is assumed.

Under AC, every sphere Beltrami coefficient with essential norm ≤k<1 has an orientation-preserving quasiconformal homeomorphic solution with prescribed coefficient and K_f=K(μ). Solutions differ exactly by Möbius postcomposition; any prescribed distinct images of 0,1,∞ determine one solution.

Under AC, the orientation-preserving K-quasiconformal sphere homeomorphisms fixing 0,1,∞ are chordally equicontinuous and compact in the uniform topology. For uniformly convergent quasiconformal sphere homeomorphisms with a homeomorphic limit, K_f≤liminf K_fn, assigning ∞ when the limit is not quasiconformal.

Under AC, each complementary component of a sphere Jordan curve admits a conformal equivalence from the disk, and every such equivalence extends uniquely to a homeomorphism of closures. Exterior normalization fixing infinity is asserted after a Möbius coordinate change making the curve finite.

Under Countable Choice, a Ck,α coefficient on a complex domain, with integer k≥0, 0<α<1 and pointwise modulus ≤k0<1, admits at every point an injective Ck+1,α local Beltrami coordinate with positive Jacobian, open image and Ck+1,α inverse.

Under Countable Choice and the stated Hölder coefficient and nondegenerate-coordinate hypotheses, every W1,2 local weak solution factors almost everywhere as H∘Φ with H holomorphic, and has a Ck+1,α local representative. Injectivity and nonvanishing of the solution derivative are not asserted.

Under AC, if K is a compact subset of a straight line or round circle and a homeomorphic embedding on an open neighborhood of K is K0-quasiconformal off K, it is K0-quasiconformal throughout that neighborhood. The corresponding sphere assertion includes generalized lines.

Under AC, for a homeomorphism of complex domains, 1-quasiconformality, local W1,2 with weak f_barz=0 almost everywhere, and biholomorphy are equivalent. The coefficient-zero reformulation for a general Sobolev homeomorphism includes the separate condition on {f_z=0}.

Under AC, an orientation-preserving L-quasisymmetric circle homeomorphism extends to a controlled quasiconformal sphere homeomorphism preserving the disk and fixing 0. The controlled converse assumes |H(0)|≤r<1. Increasing line-quasisymmetric maps extend preserving the generalized line and fixing infinity; the converse permits negating a decreasing restriction.
Under AC, for every quasiconformal sphere homeomorphism h and every compact sphere set K, K is globally conformally removable if and only if h(K) is globally conformally removable.

Under AC, every compact sphere set of finite chordal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure is globally conformally removable, including zero-length sets. Every quasicircle is globally conformally removable. No converse or dimension threshold is asserted.

Under AC, two weldings of the same h=f−1∘g differ by common Möbius postcomposition if the first curve is globally conformally removable. Consequently every quasisymmetric h has a welding curve unique up to Möbius transformation.

concerns.concern: The double-quoted sources.references locator at line 38 contains unescaped LaTeX commands. YAML decodes the alpha command to U+0007 followed by 'lpha', and the beta/bar commands to U+0008 followed by 'eta'/'ar'. The parsed source locator is corrupted; the mathematical body is unaffected.

F2 says 'Lebesgue outer measure on R² is a countably subadditive measure'; axiom_use repeats this wording. Outer measure is not a measure on arbitrary subsets. The proof uses only outer-measure subadditivity and valid covering bounds, so this is a terminology correction.
